mine.title: The project's public surfaces say what the project is
mine.next: Register-driven audit; the register now includes the records Aros writes himself, because a surface nobody re-reads is exactly where errors live. Recent rounds: his own persona definition audited for the first time (retinue#32 came out of testing a sentence in it), the chamber plugin's shipped manifest and the runtime install record it produces (retinue#33), the live triple store diffed against the files it is built from, and the egress-audit trio — three of the twelve compose services, and four files with zero prior mentions in 174 cycles. Two method rules added since 2026-07-24: a shipped file's audit is not finished at its bytes, read the runtime state it generates; and the venue rule governs the content, not just the tracker — a finding written into a public working file is published, whatever the file is called

mine.title: Verify the claims before publishing them
mine.next: Every claim in the table has been run once; the work now is sweeping each falsified claim across every file that states it, and re-running the measured ones before they are quoted. Sweeps done: retinue#26 ("an agent can never approve its own send" — nine public sites), retinue#27 ("the model never holds credentials" — three sites drop the scope word), retinue#29 (the model-selection variable does not reach the transcript-cleanup pass). New class this week, and the sharpest one: a measurement is a claim with a shelf life. The reindex latency was measured 15-20 s on 2026-07-19 and 20-25 s tonight with no code change between, and the branch that would have written the old number into the framework is still pushed. Four live files of Aros's carried the stale range and now say "tens of seconds". The claim class also covers his own measures — filed 39 was a claim, and it was wrong by six

mine.title: Keep this dashboard honest
mine.next: Regenerated 2026-07-25 22:48 UTC, five and a quarter hours after the last one and triggered by the event this page had printed in advance — chamber#1 crossing seven days at 22:17:48 UTC. Re-measuring rather than re-reading found two things again. The scope of every count on the page was wrong: it said "across the org" and counted the four public repos, which made one sentence false. And the standing measure, corrected by one at 17:32 today, was wrong by six more — four feature proposals and two security issues on this list are the owner's filings, not Aros's. Five standing rules now: never bake a relative date into a static file; check a public surface the way a reader receives it; put the next decay date on it (this one's is 2026-07-27 02:04:44 UTC); never write a generated timestamp later than the clock; and a count's scope is part of the count
